column2: the writer's notes (doubts; where the article disagrees with the entry): for the data check

The article says she lived separated from Louis at Buchsweiler, while the entry says she managed the court at Darmstadt; the place of residence is left out. The article's Issue section is empty, so the daughters' marriages are not named.
Entry ends the Company's rule in 1388; the article gives 1388-1390 for the Navarrese defeat. The end date is left out of the text.
Article also gives the defeat of Ahtum by Chanadinus; the entry calls the commander the victor, consistent. Sanjak of Çanad had an interruption 1595-1598 (Transylvania), not mentioned.
SKIPPED: article has under 250 words of substance and adds nothing beyond the existing description (Vedic panchama, Yajur-Veda origin, Faxian's account, use as an insult)
SKIPPED: article has under 250 words of substance: a lead on coca growing, a list of places and a travel warning
The article calls him Duke of Brittany from 1341; the entry says he claimed the duchy. The text says only that he fought for it.
Rouen's surrender is given as 24 June and as 23 June 1204 in the article; no day used.
The article places Chikugo in southwestern Fukuoka Prefecture; the entry says southern. Not repeated. The article says Chikugo bordered 'Higo and Chikugo' to the southeast (a slip); only Higo used.

The article states Maxtla 'named their brother, Itzcoatl, the tlatoani'; left out as unclear wording. The article's two parentages (son of Huitzilihuitl or of Acamapichtli) sit oddly with its line that he was a grandson of Acamapichtli; both versions are given as the sources' disagreement.
The article spells the brother Malek Asraf in places and Malek Ashraf in a heading; Malek Ashraf used. Baghdad Khatun is 'Baghdad Katun' in the article text and 'Baghdad Khatun' in its heading.
The article says the Ciliwung runs through two provinces, West Java and Jakarta; the 2012 clean-up plan and 2014 audit and tunnel are left out as recent administrative detail.
The article gives the founder's name as Attius Clausus; the entry has Attus Clausus. Valerius Maximus gives the form Attus, so both are attested; the text uses Attius from the article.
The article spells the scholar both H. B. Nicholson and H. B. Nicolson; Nicholson used.

The article's lead dates the design to 1808, but its body has Congreve at work from 1804 and producing 32-pounders by 1806; the year 1808 is left out. The article says Congreve later claimed not to have based his design on the Mysore rockets, while its lead and the entry say the design was based on them; the claim is left out.

The article gives two accounts of the refounding: by Drago Stipac on 25 May 1991 (lead) and by Ivan Zvonimir Čičak in 1990 (body); no founder or day used. Entry says Radić was shot in parliament in 1928; consistent.
Dates converted from the article's AD/BC to CE/BCE.

The entry names The Shop on Main Street as a New Wave film that won an Academy Award; the article says it is not considered part of the New Wave (directed by Ján Kadár and Elmar Klos, an older generation). The film is left out. The entry says the movement ended with the crushing of the Prague Spring; the article lists works up to 1970 and gives no end. No end date is given. The Joke is dated 1969 in the article's overview and 1968 in its list of key works; no year used.

Article says the kingdom was founded by northern invaders in the 14th century; entry says probably 15th: left out. Article says Gbewaa's ancestors came after the break-up of the Ghana Empire at end of 13th century: left out. 'University of Moliyili' attribution kept as the article states it.

Article says the first Mercedes models were 1902 and the 35 hp race car 1900/1901 (internally unclear); kept to 'the success of the Mercedes model'. Article's account of the 1895 re-association vs 1896 merge and 'left DMG' is loose; I used article wording. Article sentence 'Mercedes 1900/1902' inconsistencies left out.

Article: death 1000/1001 (Georgian chronicles 1001); entry says 1001: death year left out. Article: Bagrat's death 966 or 969, sole rule from 966: left as 'after Bagrat's death'. Kouropalates 977/978 and 990 left out. Article gives the 975 vs 978 date for Bagrat's Abkhazian crown inconsistently (975 anointing, 978 displacing Theodosius): used 978 only. Article says 979 for Skleros defeat consistent with entry.

Article gives reign 1508-1540; not stated to avoid mismatches. Article's 1520 Portuguese stay of six years and Bermudes' errand dates left unspecified. Article inconsistent on whether Ahmad's rebellion was ~1527 or after 1520.

Article gives birth 1474 and reign from 1480, but also says he was five in 1467 and enthroned at eight; the entry gives c. 1464: birth and accession years and age left out. Article says dates of death range 1517 to 1543; entry has 1517: death not dated.
Article says 'Shewa capitals Ankober, Angolalla'. Population is the 2007 census as given. Article's 1535 mustering vs 'twice' left as is.
Article dates founding 294 BC; entry says c. 293 BCE: founding year left out.
Entry says Lacy built the castle from 1282; article says Edward I ordered the castle and walls begun in 1282 and granted the lordship to Lacy in 1284. Text avoids saying who built it.
Article gives 965 seizure of power and 968 imperial title, consistent with entry. Article says Song annexed Southern Han in 971.
SKIPPED: article under about 250 words of substance; adds little beyond the description
Article has Stephen meeting Pepin at Ponthion (6 Jan 754) and also says in the intro the promise was at Quierzy in April 754; text follows the Background/Original promise sections.
Article says reign four years and also three years; length of reign left out. Article's two birth names given as alternatives; used Nguyễn Phúc Ưng Kỷ as the article's enthronement text does.

Article says 'region of Po' for park funder; rendered 'the region'. Desc says Taurini lived at the confluence; article doesn't say so: not repeated. Desc says route used since antiquity: not in article, not repeated.
SKIPPED: article under about 250 words of substance and adds nothing to the description beyond Herodotus's expulsion story already told
Article says Olympic committee presidency of 'West Germany' (intro) vs 'Germany' (body); used Germany. He was invited to the 1960 Togo independence celebration: omitted.

Article gives his death date as 22 and 23 October 1893; omitted. Article says he was exiled in 1854 but deposed 'at 15' in the intro; used the body's dates. Article says pension 120,000 rupees (£50,000).

Reign dates for Kubrat and Asparuh given variously in article (632-668, c.632-665, 681-701); omitted. Article's sentence on Old Great Bulgaria 632-668 vs Kubrat c.632-665 inconsistent. Legacy (Dulo Hill) omitted.
Entry's claim about the Xiongnu in the 1st century BCE is not in the article and was not repeated. Economic share figures and cooperative loan details omitted as indices/policy.
SKIPPED: article is about the present-day administrative unit (census figures, economy, districts) and says nothing of the history in the description; too little lasting material

Article: death 680 or 681 and 'assassinated in 681'; entry has c. 681: date left out. Article gives 658 start and also 659 election: text says 658 'first from 658' and 'in 659 elected' — slight article inconsistency; entry says about 658.
Article calls the 685 battle Nechtansmere / Dun Nechtain, sited at Dunnichen or Dunachton; left out the Nechtansmere name. Article says Ecgfrith lost Lindsey 679 after Trent; entry agrees.

Two sections only: the source has nothing on the province today beyond its correspondence to Niigata Prefecture, given in Setting. Entry's details on Kenshin's Kasugayama, ramie and Nagaoka are not in the source; not repeated. Only mention of Kenshin is the 1562 temple move.

Two sections: the source says nothing of the province today beyond its correspondence to northern Fukui Prefecture. The entry says Nobunaga destroyed the Asakura in 1573; the article gives no year, so none is printed.
Article dates edict 29 Oct 1685; entry says October 1685: consistent. Entry says many settled in Berlin: not in article, left out.
Entry says High King proclaimed 1316; article says proclaimed 1315 and crowned 1316; no year given for the proclamation in the text. Article on his marriage dispensation 1317 left out.

The article's lead says he taught in Sierra Leone for five years in the early twentieth century; the body gives 1901-1906 directing Muslim education, which is what is printed. Further cut: his marriage to Sarah Yates and his later family with Anna Erskine.
The article spells the palace Phillipsburg; that spelling is kept. Left out: the cultural references (Byron, Turner, Melville, Digby) and the Deutsches Eck.
Article says Gomez died 17 Dec 1935; entry consistent. Article says 'selected to succeed', entry says succeeded.

Entry says electronic machines nationwide from 2004 and first election 1951-52 with 173 million voters; neither is in the article (article: phased since late 1990s), so omitted. Left out the article's comment on the 2023 law's effect (assessment).
Entry says crowned without regalia: not in article, omitted. Article lists Southern Court's eras Shōhei/Kentoku, left out.
The excerpt gives no year for Hou Jing's capture of Jiankang or for the start of the civil war against Xiao Baojuan (the entry says 501), so neither year is printed.
Article gives the Taixing era 318 and death 3 January 323; entry gives 318 and 323, consistent. Article says posted to Jianye in 307; entry says same.

The article calls the warlord Zhu Quanzhong in the body and Zhu Wen in the lead; Zhu Wen is used throughout, as in the entry. The entry says Li Maozhen held the emperor at Fengxiang until Zhu's siege forced a handover in 903; the excerpt's Fengxiang section breaks off before that, so it is left out. The earlier draft said the prince had his own attendant whipped; the article says Tian Lingzi whipped the attendant. Corrected.

The entry says Nevada, Illinois and Virginia ratified between 2017 and 2020; the article names the three states but gives no years in the excerpt, so no years are printed for them. Left out: the Washington Post's criticism of Biden's declaration (a verdict on a recent leader) and the details of each lawsuit.
Consistent with the entry: the Concordat of 1801, the Congress of Vienna and retirement on Pius VII's death in 1823.

The entry names the Seeberg observatory; the article calls it the Observatory of Gotha and does not name Seeberg, so no site name is printed. The article does not say in words who succeeded him, so no successor is named.

The article contradicts itself on Goda: the Career section says he repudiated her when he married Ida, the family section that she died about 1047 and he remarried soon after. Neither version is printed. The article gives 1049 as the start of his rule as count; the entry's 'from about 1049' is left unrepeated.

The article dates his promotion to field marshal to November 1758 but tells it in its Minden section; no date is printed for the promotion. The article gives 12 June 1758 for Rheinberg and no date for Krefeld; Krefeld is left undated.

Left out the present holder (the article names General Sir Gwyn Jenkins as holder now). The entry's Prince Louis of Battenberg resignation in 1914 is not in the article beyond his being First Sea Lord in 1914; not repeated.

The article says the pirates formed the Flying Gang around 1715; the entry dates it 1716-1718. No year is printed for its formation. The article dates the news of the pardon to 1717 in one place and has Pearse sailing in March 1718 in another; no date is printed for Pearse.
Article says the fort was founded 1639 (and Day's negotiations in 1639); entry says begun 1640. Both founding years left out.
Fielding and Bylandt affair year 1779 inferred from the article's context (November 1779 order, convoy sailed in December).
Article says Austria declared Parma a fief of Milan; entry says nothing on it. Article calls Francesco 'seventh Farnese Duke'; omitted. 'Death and legacy' used as death date given.
Article gives execution 29 October 1799; entry says executed when the monarchy was restored that summer: not contradicted (restoration in summer, execution later).
SKIPPED: article has under 250 words of substance beyond the entry (mostly a list of orders and decorations)
Article says he ruled 1806-07 and 1813-15; consistent with desc.
Article does not mention the 1831 constitution quarrel or the 1850 crisis explicitly; only Hassenpflug's reinstatement in 1850. Desc says sole ruler from 1847; article says Prince-elector 1847. Fine.
Entry says Kabylia subdued 1857 and independence 1962; article has neither, omitted. Article gives Constantine siege as 1837.
Article says first sung at Quisisana Hotel; entry says Turco prompted it perhaps as a joke; not repeated.

Entry says the region 'was ruled by branches of the Griffin dukes'; the article does not name the Griffins, not used. Entry gives 1653 transfer, article too. The article's 'Treaty of Stettin (1630)' used.

Article gives death 4 August 1378 in the lead and 4 August 1379 later; 1378 used, as in the entry. Article puts the castle's commissioning in 1350 (before Pavia was taken in 1359) and its completion in 1363; castle dates left out. Article spells both Querasima and Quaresima. Peace treaty with Gregory XI dated spring 1375 in one place and spring 1378 in another: no date given.
Entry says record majority in 1962; article gives only the figures, so 'record' omitted. Article gives death cause two ways (paralytic ileus and lung infection; lung failure): omitted.
Article gives reign 1181-1221, consistent with entry's late 12th-early 13th century. Article says Lalibela was born 1162 while also reigning from 1181; fine.

SKIPPED: the entry is about the gentry of Ming China; the saved article is the general concept, mostly on Europe and Britain, with only a short passage on China's four divisions of society, so it does not support a text on the Ming gentry Entry and article are different subjects (Ming gentry versus gentry in general).
Article does not mention King Munza or Azande by name; omitted. Article gives English edition 1873 and German 1874 as printed.
Article says tower built around 1130 with the cathedral; entry says begun end of 11th century. Both left out. Height (86.12 m) vs entry's about 87 m: left out.
Entry says the present keep is a 1956 reconstruction; article says the 1950s; date omitted. Article says 'Yoshiyasu' once for Yoshitatsu; used Yoshitatsu.

Article given in part. Entry says the Vastupala-Tejapala shrines are 13th century; inscriptions of 1230 agree. Article dates the Neminatha temple to 1128 AD and also says the 10th-century idol temple was renovated by Sajjana in the 12th century: the 1128 date left out. The dispute between Jains and followers of Dattatreya over the highest peak (court cases pending) left out as a matter still going on.
Entry says he passed a law giving Latin rights to Transpadane Gaul; article does not mention it, omitted. Article lead says 'c. 135 - 87 BC'.

Article contradicts itself: the lead says the Church was freed from all taxes, the list of articles says taxes may be levied on the Church; left out. The list says noblemen 'may be arbitrarily arrested but not oppressed' (garbled), while the entry says freedom from arbitrary arrest: arrest left out. Article dates the charter to the seventeenth year of Andrew's reign, with Andrew's accession in 1205 (his chancellery later counted from 1204).
SKIPPED: article has under 250 words of substance: geography, farm figures and a list of tourist sites; nothing on Daegaya's history beyond the entry

Entry says 1723 to 1730; the source says 1723-1729 for the conversion, so the end year is left out. Source calls it the largest treasure collection in Europe; the entry says one of the largest, so no superlative is printed. Estimated value of the 2019 theft left out.

Entry says the company was merged with rival firms after his death and chartered by Paul I in 1799; the source says only that the assets were merged with the royal Russian-American Company in 1799, so the charter and 'rival firms' are not printed. Source gives the old-style death date 20 July.
Entry says she is credited as the most famous female painter; not repeated. Skipped the poem anecdotes (Song of You and Me) as the source retells them twice with slight differences.
Entry says the Gediz is the ancient Hermus; the source does not, so it is not printed. Port rankings, the bridge project and most shipwreck details omitted.
Entry says Gorkha kingdom armies and Buddhist, shamanic and Hindu practices; source names neither the kingdom's armies nor Hindu practice, so not printed.
Source gives 1200-1260 and an Antwerp birth; the entry says fl. 13th century and probably Antwerp or Brussels, so no birth or death dates or birthplace printed.
Source says the Dutch surrendered in February 1942 (usually March); date left out. Source says he was disillusioned with Suharto's authoritarianism; left out as an assessment, only the facts told.

Entry says commissioner from 1891; source says Commissioner and Consul-general for Mozambique and Nyasa districts from 1888/9, so the 1889 arrival is told without the title. Johnston Falls, school etc left out.
Entry dates the burning of the camps to 203 BCE; source gives no year beyond Scipio's 204 BCE landing, so the year is left out.

Entry says Zanzibar became a protectorate 'later that year'; source says 'immediately'; the text says 'soon'. Source says Germany 'gained' Wituland protectorate handover; entry says claims in Witu given up; text says protectorate handed over.

Source says he became adviser to Kumarapala in 1125 and was introduced to Siddharaja probably around 1125; the two cannot both hold, so no year is given for either. Death year differs by source (1172/1173), left out as entry gives 1173. Source claims Jainism became the official religion of Gujarat; left out as an unqualified claim.
Entry gives c. 1188 for birth; source says 1187, so no birth year is printed. Entry says chronicle covers events to 1227; source does not say, left out. Source thin (about 330 words).

Entry says 'of Armenian origin'; source says this is a disputed deduction from a misread passage of Theophylact, so no origin is printed. Entry says nephew Nicetas sent overland to Egypt; source does not say, left out. Source: Africa appointment before 602; 'around 600' in the lead.

Source says the Franco state ended in 1975 and the government in exile dissolved in 1977. The date of the Prague match is given as 1 October 1967 for the 1968 championship; the source's own wording. Lyrics not quoted: the source's lyric sections are empty and the satirical verses are crude.
The Histiaeus 'King of Miletus' wording in the source left out. Nearly all of the account rests on Herodotus, as the text says.
SKIPPED: article has under 250 words of substance: a few sentences on the capital, Mito Castle and two history books, the rest a list of districts; a longer text would be padding

Entry's Tecumseh and Tippecanoe 1811 not in source, so not repeated. Source gives conflicting accounts of the lost warriors (Lake Michigan, Lake Winnebago); text says 'a storm on a lake'. Nation population given as source's 'about 12,000'.

Entry says the guesthouse developed into the palace; the source dates this to the 15th century. The legend of the hart is told as legend. Royal Vault list shortened. Restoration proposals of 1835 and 1906 left out for length.

The source's counts of recipients (seven in Canada, eight in the United States) are already in the entry and not repeated. Berlin's award to Clay dated 1962 as the source words it; Gorbachev's year not given.
Article is mostly a title list; kept to 3 short sections. Article calls the last king Martin the Humanist, desc Martin the Humane: epithet left out.
Article says the castle was built in 1141 and given to Barisan in 1141; desc says around 1141: year left out of the text. Heraldry section (film Kingdom of Heaven) left out.
Article gives rebellion as 874-884 and 'mid-870s'; desc says 875: dates for the rising left out. Article calls him salt trader; desc salt smuggler.
Article mentions Dec 2025 stupas at Zehanpora in Kashmir possibly linked to a lost city Huvishkapura: left out (recent, tentative).
Article does not mention Seleucus I as commander; desc's claim not repeated.

Desc dates contest of Itō/Ōtomo/Shimazu to 16th c. and Mimikawa 1578 (not in article); article places the contest in the Nanboku-chō period and has Shimazu surrender 1587. Mimikawa left out; both left unreconciled.

SKIPPED: article has under 250 words of substance, nearly all already in the description (teachers, al-Nujum al-zahira, al-Manhal al-safi, the continuation of al-Maqrizi); the rest is a list of titles and editions
Article does not say Fez founded by him, nor the Sulaymanid grant at Tlemcen, nor 'quarters' (desc); not repeated.
Left out: politics, media, sport, tourism details, 2010 road accident, 1990 ceremonial lord.
Desc: 1493, line in the Atlantic; consistent. Article describes three bulls dated 3-4 May; the line is in the third (4 May). Piis fidelium and Dudum siquidem left out for length.
Article gives death as 18 December 1826 and the plaque text 17 December: death day left out. Article says forgeries began 1777-; desc says Dafydd poems 1789.
Article is on the movement; text drawn from it. Desc says third bill 'passed in 1914' consistent.
Desc order 'Saltukids before Seljuks of Rum' kept consistent: article has Saltukids until 1124, Georgians, then Seljuk recapture 1201-1225. Neighbourhood list, mayor, climate, economy left out.
Article says 100 Japanese set sail; also 48 administrators and 53 students and attendants (article inconsistent); used 'about 100'.
Article is short; desc says he led Ghent from 1338, article says he entered politics in 1337: no year given for his entry.

Desc says he founded Batavia 1619; article says he reconquered Jakarta in 1619 and the city was renamed Batavia in 1621; wording kept to the article's. Article lead says 1,700 enslaved; body says 800 deported: lead's figure left out.
Article spells the battle Chirokitia, desc Khirokitia: battle not named. Article gives the tax as based on income from 5,000 duchies (probably ducats): figure left out.
Article's discussion of China's claim over succession left out as present-day politics.
Desc says murdered in 'Kaegyong'; article says Gaeseong. Desc spells Yi Seong-gye; article Yi Sŏng-gye.
The article says the cognomen Cicero was given after his death and that his eloquence is debatable; the entry says it referred to his reputed eloquence. Worded so as not to contradict.
SKIPPED: article has under 250 words of substance beyond the entry (conversion, Herrenhausen, Sartorio, daughters)
Entry: led the Australian Corps from May 1918; article: became commander in May 1918, promotion confirmed 1 June 1918. Date left out of the text.
Article says his grandson Rafael Yglesias Castro was president 1894-1902; left out (relationship via daughter Cristina Fernández Castro is muddled in the article).
The article quotes a 1940 article of his praising Hitler; not included, as only the Franco sympathy is stated in the article's own voice.

Article contradicts itself on Capítulos que se le olvidaron a Cervantes: published posthumously in 1895 vs dated 1868 in the works list; date left out. Article says exiled to Colombia for seven years; length left out.
Article says he took part in the negotiations leading to the Compromise of 1867; entry says he accepted it. Left out.
Article: Strabo's 'one-eyed Candace' dated 23 BCE in one place and the Amanirenas attack 25 BC in another; used only the 25 BCE attack date.
Entry: about 50 km south-west of Prayagraj; article: about 56 km southwest of the confluence at Prayaga. Distance left out.
Article says he was aided against the Tatars by 'his son Yasukai', but elsewhere makes Yesugei his grandson; left out.
Article gives the Khongirad of Khiva as 1717-1920 in one place and 1763-1920 in another; both left out.
Article gives his death as 996/78 BC; not printed. The entry's Xiao Yu ding and Guifang victory are not in the article.
The Xinian account (recognised only in 741 BCE, moved to Chengzhou 738 BCE) sits uneasily with the entry's reign 770-720 BCE; given as the manuscript's challenge, attributed.
Article gives reign 977/75 BC to 957 BC; entry says late tenth century. Exact reign dates left out.

Article is thin; Bukit Melawati section is empty in the article so the fort is not described. Entry says seat of the first sultans; the article only says capital in the early years of the 18th century, so wording kept general. Film titles are only listed under In popular culture.

Article dates: died c. 1375 BC, Dur-Kurigalzu c. 1390 BC; consistent with the entry's early 14th century BCE. The battle site Dur-Shulgi is left unnamed (the article's spelling is garbled). Excavation years 1942-45 given as 'began in 1942'.

Article's legal case is 'still ongoing' with no date: told only as legal action taken. Entry's 'more than 200 armed followers' not in the article; not repeated. Article: 68 deaths; entry: dozens killed: consistent.

Article says the resolution formed the basis for the League's decision in 1946 to struggle for one state; entry says it became the basis of the demand for Pakistan: not repeated with a date. Article is partisan in places (Congress 'atrocities'); written as the League's propaganda. The intimidation claim is stated as the article states it.

Article says Lake Palace and Pichola Lake were built by Rana Lakshasimha in 1362 and the palace rebuilt 1743-1746; left out as it conflicts with the entry's 1743-1746 build. Article says IHCL has managed the hotel for 50 years while also saying Taj took over in 1971: left out. Heading 'What it is' used for description and the 1857 episode.
Children's number left out: the article says thirteen children, eleven surviving at the arrest, but also 3 sons and 9 daughters. Place of the wedding (Spires/Speyer) left out.
Article dates Mangrai's conquest to 1281; the entry says 1292. Year left out of the text per rule. Article's Wiang Kum Kam sentence follows the conquest.
Entry's August 1920 recognition by Soviet Russia is not in the article, so not used.

Article says the 1377 copy was commissioned by Dionysius of Suzdal; entry says Prince Dmitry Konstantinovich. The patron is left out of the text. Article says years 898-922, 1263-1283 and 1288-1294 were omitted for censorship; but also says leaves are lost; the two accounts are not both printed. Article's 'second edition of Nestor's chronicle' wording kept as 'second edition of the Primary Chronicle' - check. Article calls the year range of gap 898-921 and 898-922 inconsistently; text gives 898 to 921 only.
Article gives the frontier's span as about 83 to 260 AD but says the district was lost about 250; only the 250 loss is printed.

Article says both 'sandstone' (lead) and 'marble' (Description); material left out. Lion posture debated (standing per Oertel, seated per Abdullaev 2014); 'back to back' kept only in the entry. Entry says adopted 1950 as emblem; article gives cabinet acceptance on 29 December 1947; neither date printed for the emblem. Excavation year (entry 1905, article winter 1904-05) left out of the text.

Article does not describe the Rainhill Trials; the entry's mention of them is not expanded. Article questions the 'inter-city' label (city status 1853 and 1880); not raised, as the entry uses it. Article does not say Huskisson died the same day; not stated.
Article calls the Schlosstheater 'Europe's oldest theater'; left out as doubtful and unsourced in the text. Headings changed to the list for a work.
Entry mentions land grants from Swazi kings; not in the article, not used. Article calls it centre of fly-fishing industry; left out.

Article gives the 1983 inquiry's cash figure as $57.3 million and, in a New York Times quotation, unexplained deposits of $3.5 million: no figure printed. Article: PLP leader 1956-1997; entry: governed until 1992: consistent.

Article gives birth 1104 and the Battle of Saveh in September 1118; entry gives birth 1105 and Saveh 1119. Birth year, age and battle year left out. Article says he ruled 'Iraq and Persia'. Article lists several wives and children: omitted.
Article says 110 km east of Tutuila, entry about 100 km: distance left out. Entry says park land also on Ofu; article names only Alei on Taʻū: Ofu not mentioned.

Article: called for overthrow on 14 December 1845, Herrera resigned 30 December 1845; entry: coup in January 1846. December dates left out. Article: resigned 28 July 1846, captured after the revolt of 3 August; entry: overthrown in August 1846. Resignation date left out. Entry says the revolt restored the Constitution of 1824; article says 'the Federal System': kept as the article words it. Entry's 'refused to negotiate' not printed.

Entry says James was born in Montpellier and that she died while defending the marriage before the Pope; the article gives no birthplace and says she died on her way back to Aragon after the Pope's decision. Neither point printed beyond the article's words; James's birth date (article 1 February 1208) left out to avoid a second date beside the entry's. Article gives birth 1182; entry c. 1182: birth year not printed.
Entry's Julius Maternus is not in the article; not mentioned. Article spells al-Mas'udi with diacritics; plain form used. His death is not told, so the last heading is Legacy.
Article gives no date for the 1920s British rule or French resistance mentioned in the entry; left out. Left out the genetics section.
Article has the confirmation ceremony on 13 July and the convention on 13 July; I told only the convention.
Article's lead says 'four provinces' counting Harare; I wrote three plus Harare, consistent with the history section. Left out its judgement on the economy.
The entry says Welsh and Breton traditions; article agrees. Article's author lists were empty.
The article gives the deaths of Sæberht and Æthelberht as around 616 or 618 (lead: around 616); the entry says around 616. The year is left out of the text.

Entry says about 190 km; article 117 miles (188 km): did not print length. Entry says it flows 'south then east'; article says north-east. Entry says the river 'flows into the Atlantic'; article says Gulf of Maine. I used the article's wording. Entry mentions Abenaki communities, not in article; left out. Left out current pollution concerns.
Article gives death as 1266/68; the entry says c. 1268; I wrote 'in or shortly before 1268' per the article's later text. Article says Michael ruled from 1230; entry says about 1230.
Article: presidency Feb 1859 to Dec 1860; entry says 1859 to 1860, consistent. Entry says 'one of the youngest'; article 27 at the time; not repeated.

Article dates the marble Tipitaka to 1868, before the Fifth Buddhist Council of 1871; the entry ties the inscription to the council. Year left out. Article says he is one of the most revered kings; not repeated. Article calls Mindon 'penultimate king'; entry says second-last, consistent.

Entry says Mir Qasim replaced him in 1760 and he was restored in 1763; article's body says he was installed again in 1764 after Buxar, while its lead has him restored before Mir Qasim went to war. Text follows the lead's order without a year. Dates of replacement and restoration left out; entry's 1760/1763 not printed. Article lead says Siraj's rule 'tyrannical' - attributed only via Clive's quote, which I paraphrased as 'universally hated'.

Entry says passed to the Greek Patriarchate in 1685 and calls the fresco 'said to portray' Rustaveli; article calls it a portrait (legendary poet). Entry names the builder Giorgi-Prokhore; article names Prochorus the Iberian: same person presumably. Entry says 'for centuries centre of Georgian learning' not in article; omitted.
Article says Jikji 1377 'Goryeo'. Entry says 'eleventh century'; article 'around 1040', consistent.
